source.title: Zero-Temperature Dynamics of Ising Spin Systems Following a Deep Quench: Results and Open Problems

accepted.question_text: Consider a zero-temperature stochastic Ising spin system with nearest-neighbor Hamiltonian H = −∑Jxy σxσy, initial spin configuration σ0 drawn from the symmetric Bernoulli product measure, and standard continuous-time single-spin-flip Glauber dynamics: energy-lowering flips are accepted, energy-increasing flips are rejected, and zero-energy flips are accepted with probability 1/2. For homogeneous ferromagnets or homogeneous antiferromagnets on Zd, or on any other lattice not already covered by the odd-number-of-neighbors type-F result, in dimension d ≥ 3, what is the dynamical outcome? Equivalently, is the system type I, meaning almost every site flips infinitely many times; type F, meaning almost every site flips only finitely many times; or type M, meaning both finitely flipping and infinitely flipping sites have strictly positive spatial density?
accepted.context_brief: Homogeneous Ising dynamics in dimension at least three

evidence.quote: Consider the stochastic process σ t = σ t(ω ) corresponding to the zero-temperature limit of Glauber dynamics for an Ising model with Hamiltonian, H = − ∑ Jx,y σxσy .
The initial spin configuration σ 0 is chosen from a symmetric Bernoulli product measure (denoted Pσ 0), corresponding physically to a deep quench.

The densities ρF and ρI depend only on d, µ, and possibly lattice type, and of course satisfy ρF + ρI = 1. We characterize the triplet ( d, µ , lattice type) as being type F or I or M (for mixed) according to whether ρF = 1 or ρI = 1 or 0 < ρ F , ρ I < 1.

For Ising spin systems with Hamiltonian (1), and J , σ 0 and ω chosen as discussed in Sec. 1, the problems of the dynamical outcomes of the following situations remain open: 1) Homogeneous ferromagnets (and antiferromagnets) on the lattice Zd (or others except where each site has an odd number of neighbors) for d ≥ 3. Numerical results [2] suggest that these should be type I for d = 3 and perhaps 4, but may possibly be type F (or M) for d ≥ 5.

accepted.question_text: Consider a zero-temperature stochastic Ising spin system with nearest-neighbor Hamiltonian H = −∑Jxy σxσy, initial spin configuration σ0 drawn from the symmetric Bernoulli product measure, and standard continuous-time single-spin-flip Glauber dynamics. Suppose the nearest-neighbor couplings are drawn from a continuous disorder distribution in dimension d > 1, the coupling distribution has infinite mean, and influence percolation occurs. What is the dynamical outcome: type F, where almost every site flips only finitely many times, or type M, where finitely flipping and infinitely flipping sites both have strictly positive spatial density?
accepted.context_brief: Continuous-disorder Ising dynamics with infinite mean

evidence.quote: Consider the stochastic process σ t = σ t(ω ) corresponding to the zero-temperature limit of Glauber dynamics for an Ising model with Hamiltonian, H = − ∑ Jx,y σxσy .
The initial spin configuration σ 0 is chosen from a symmetric Bernoulli product measure (denoted Pσ 0), corresponding physically to a deep quench.

The densities ρF and ρI depend only on d, µ, and possibly lattice type, and of course satisfy ρF + ρI = 1. We characterize the triplet ( d, µ , lattice type) as being type F or I or M (for mixed) according to whether ρF = 1 or ρI = 1 or 0 < ρ F , ρ I < 1.

What about models where the disorder is continuous but the mean is infinite? We can show that a restricted class of these models are type F ; these are models where influence percolation [15] does not occur.

2) Models with continuous disorder in d > 1, where both the coupling distribution has infinite mean and influence percolation occurs. The proof [13] sketched in Sec. 4 already implies that ρF > 0 for these models, so they are either type F or M. It seems reasonable to conjecture that they are type F .

accepted.question_text: Consider a zero-temperature stochastic ±J Ising spin system with nearest-neighbor Hamiltonian H = −∑Jxy σxσy, initial spin configuration σ0 drawn from the symmetric Bernoulli product measure, and standard continuous-time single-spin-flip Glauber dynamics, where each coupling takes one of two opposite nonzero values J1 and J2 with J1 = −J2. On Zd, or on another lattice not already covered by the odd-number-of-neighbors type-F result, in dimension d ≥ 3, what is the dynamical outcome? In particular, is the ±J system type I, type F, or type M, and can the density ρF of finitely flipping sites in the ±J model be related to the corresponding density in the homogeneous ferromagnet on the same lattice?

evidence.quote: Consider the stochastic process σ t = σ t(ω ) corresponding to the zero-temperature limit of Glauber dynamics for an Ising model with Hamiltonian, H = − ∑ Jx,y σxσy .
The initial spin configuration σ 0 is chosen from a symmetric Bernoulli product measure (denoted Pσ 0), corresponding physically to a deep quench.

The densities ρF and ρI depend only on d, µ, and possibly lattice type, and of course satisfy ρF + ρI = 1. We characterize the triplet ( d, µ , lattice type) as being type F or I or M (for mixed) according to whether ρF = 1 or ρI = 1 or 0 < ρ F , ρ I < 1.
When J1 = − J2 ≠ 0, we call this a ± J model. (In much of the literature, ± J spin glasses refer to the specific case α = 1 / 2.)

3) ± J models on Zd (or other lattices except where each site has an odd number of neighbors) for d ≥ 3. There is little we can say about these right now, except that it would be interesting to relate ± J models to homogeneous ferromagnets on the same lattice. E.g., perhaps ρF (± J model)≥ ρF (homogeneous ferromagnet). If this were the case, then demonstrating that homogeneous ferromagnets are type F on Zd for d ≥ 5 would immediately resolve the question for ± J spin glasses on those lattices.

accepted.question_text: For Ising spin glasses at positive temperature in dimension d ≥ 3, does local non-equilibration occur? Here local non-equilibration means that, on finite length scales, the system does not equilibrate into a pure state after a finite time; equivalently, interfaces do not permanently cease moving across the finite region. The question depends on the unknown number and structure of positive-temperature pure states in these spin glasses; from a rigorous viewpoint the corresponding pure-state structure is not even proved in dimension d = 2.
accepted.context_brief: Positive-temperature local non-equilibration in spin glasses

evidence.quote: Without going into detail, we will simplify matters here by dividing systems into those where on any finite lengthscale, the system equilibrates (into a pure state) after a finite time (depending on σ 0, ω , the lengthscale, and J if relevant), in the sense that interfaces cease to move across the region after that time; and those where this local equilibration does not occur. The latter case we call local non-equilibration (LNE)

Because the number and structure of pure states at positive temperature in Ising spin glasses is unknown for d ≥ 3 (and, from a rigorous point of view, unproved even for d = 2), occurrence of LNE there remains an open question.

evidence.quote: In particular, throughout this paper we have concerned ourselves solely with the question of convergence of σ t (with P -probability one) to a final state, but have not examined the properties of this final state (when it exists) in the different models of interest. We also have not discussed rates of convergence to the final state.
